title: Multi-factor authentication flow
description: Authentication requires two or more independent factors: something known (password), something held (one-time code), or something inherent (biometric). The factors must be independent so compromising one does not compromise the others. Step-up authentication adds factors for sensitive actions. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers combining password with a one-time code.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ("correct", "123456"), 2: ("correct", "000000"), 3: ("wrong", "123456")}
pw, otp = CFG[LEVEL]
pw_ok = (pw == "correct")
otp_ok = (otp == "123456")
print("password:", "ok" if pw_ok else "FAIL", "| one-time code:", "ok" if otp_ok else "FAIL", "| authenticated:", pw_ok and otp_ok)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Password hashing with salt
description: Passwords are never stored directly: each is combined with a unique random salt and run through a slow key-derivation function like PBKDF2, bcrypt, or Argon2. Verification re-derives the hash and compares in constant time. Salts defeat rainbow tables; slowness defeats brute force. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers unique random salt per password.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 1000, 2: 10000, 3: 60000}
import hashlib, os, hmac
salt = os.urandom(16)
dk = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", b"s3cret", salt, CFG[LEVEL])
guess = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", b"s3cret", salt, CFG[LEVEL])
print("iterations:", CFG[LEVEL], "| verify:", hmac.compare_digest(dk, guess))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Token-based session management
description: After authentication the server issues a signed session token carrying the identity and expiry. Each request presents the token; the server verifies the signature and expiry without a database lookup. Tokens are short-lived and refreshable, and revocation lists kill compromised sessions. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers signed tokens carrying identity and expiry.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 3600, 2: 600, 3: 60}
import hashlib, hmac, time
SECRET = b"session-secret"
def issue(user, ttl):
    body = "%s|%d" % (user, int(time.time()) + ttl)
    return body + "|" + hmac.new(SECRET, body.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16]
def verify(tok):
    body, sig = tok.rsplit("|", 1)
    user, exp = body.split("|")
    good = hmac.compare_digest(sig, hmac.new(SECRET, body.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16])
    return good and int(exp) > time.time()
tok = issue("amy", CFG[LEVEL])
print("ttl=%ds token valid:" % CFG[LEVEL], verify(tok))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Account recovery with verification
description: Account recovery requires proof through a verified channel plus a cooldown before the recovered account regains full privileges. Recovery codes are single-use and the old credentials are invalidated. Every recovery is logged and the account owner is notified through all channels. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers verified-channel proof plus cooldown.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"code_ok": True, "hours": 25}, 2: {"code_ok": True, "hours": 5}, 3: {"code_ok": False, "hours": 30}}
c = CFG[LEVEL]
ok = c["code_ok"] and c["hours"] >= 24
print("code valid:", c["code_ok"], "| cooldown %dh:" % c["hours"], "met" if c["hours"] >= 24 else "NOT met", "| recovered:", ok)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
